indicator: Equity Valuations (Earnings/Price minus 10y Treasury yield)
construction: Shiller E/P (ie_data.xls) minus FRED DGS10, quarterly mean

indicator: Equity Valuations (Earnings/Price ratio)
construction: Shiller E/P (ie_data.xls), quarterly mean

indicator: Indicators of Volatility (VIX)
construction: FRED VIXCLS quarterly mean (log applied at index stage)

indicator: Indicators of Volatility (CDS premium)
construction: Paper uses Markit IG CDS premia (proprietary). Public analog: Moody's Baa credit spread, the standard public investment-grade credit-spread gauge (same convention round 1 used for the BBB-spread indicator). Excess bond premium conceptually closer but takes negative values, breaking the pipeline log transform; GZ spread scored lower (0.898 vs 0.955).
caveat: Quarterly mean of monthly BAA minus quarterly mean of daily DGS10, in percentage points. Accessible CDS series covers 2005Q2-2014Q4 (39 quarters); proxy scored on that overlap. Rejected: total credit spread variant (corr 0.898); level-shifted excess bond premium (0.820; shift arbitrary and still strained under log).

indicator: Spread of Corporate Bonds over Treasuries (BBB)
construction: FRED BAA (Moody's Baa yield) minus DGS10, quarterly mean, pp
caveat: Paper uses ICE BofA BBB OAS (bp); Moody's Baa spread is the public analog

indicator: Spread of Corporate Bonds over Treasuries (High Yield)
construction: Monthly Moody's Baa-Treasury spread plus monthly EBP, averaged to quarterly. HY OAS = IG spread + extra default/liquidity compensation; EBP isolates the credit-risk premium. Replaces the Baa-only proxy (corr 0.72 -> 0.86).

indicator: Investor Appetite for Risky Corporate Debt (junk + leveraged loan issuance)
construction: Paper uses HY bond + leveraged loan issuance (Dealogic/LCD, proprietary; SIFMA public quarterly history truncated to recent quarters; no public quarterly leveraged-loan issuance exists). Proxy: inverse average corporate credit spread - when credit spreads are tight, investor appetite for risky debt is strong and issuance surges; a standard risk-appetite gauge. Raw = 1/(GZ spread in %).
caveat: Quarterly mean of monthly GZ spread, inverted. Accessible issuance series covers 2002Q1-2014Q4 (52 quarters). Rejected: 1/VIX (0.818); 1/Baa spread (0.588); Z.1 net corporate bond issuance (0.284 - IG issuance surged in 2008-09 while HY collapsed); 1/expected-default prob (0.665).

indicator: Investor Appetite for Risky Corporate Debt (C&I lending standards)
construction: FRED DRTSCILM (net % tightening, large/middle-market firms)

indicator: Prices for Commercial Real Estate (CRE)
construction: BIS US quarterly commercial property price index, nominal, as published (index level). Paper applies 10y-MA detrend; level/base differences wash out in transform.

indicator: Change in Lending Standards, CRE Loans
construction: Net % of domestic banks tightening standards for CRE loans. 1990Q2-2013Q2: discontinued aggregate series SUBLPDRCS_N.Q ('All commercial real estate loans'), re-dated back one quarter to match paper's reference-quarter convention (paper dates each survey to the quarter it asks about; corr=1.0000 over 90 quarters). 2013Q3-2014Q4: splice using mean of the three successor sub-questions (construction & land development SUBLPDRCSC_N.Q, nonfarm nonresidential SUBLPDRCSN_N.Q, multifamily SUBLPDRCSM_N.Q), same dating. Paper's exact post-split splice not reverse-engineered.

indicator: National House Prices Relative to Rents
construction: FRED CSUSHPISA / CUSR0000SEHA (rent of primary residence CPI)

indicator: Mortgage Lending and FICO Scores (FICO scores)
construction: Annual UPB-weighted mean origination FICO for GSE (Fannie Mae) single-family acquisitions; cubic-spline interpolated from annual (mid-year) to quarterly. Concept matches paper: 'FICO scores for mortgages sold to GSEs.'

indicator: Mortgage Lending and FICO Scores (change in lending standards)
construction: FRED DRTSPM (prime mortgages, from 2007)
caveat: Paper uses all-residential SLOOS from 1990; DRTSPM covers prime only from 2007Q2

indicator: Real Debt Growth of Nonfinancial Businesses
construction: y/y % change of GDP-deflated total nonfinancial business debt

indicator: Risky Debt of Nonfinancial Businesses (net leverage of risky firms)
construction: 100 * (nonfinancial corporate business debt securities and loans) / (total assets), quarterly NSA levels. Aggregate net-leverage analogue of the paper's Compustat-based net leverage of speculative-grade/unrated firms. Alternatives tested and rejected: net-of-checkable-deposits version (corr 0.743) and the excess bond premium EBP (quarterly avg, corr 0.243).

indicator: Risky Debt of Nonfinancial Businesses (deep junk issuance share)
construction: Paper uses CCC-or-below share of HY issuance (no public quarterly series exists - SIFMA does not break HY out by rating; loan/bond deal databases are proprietary). Proxy: negated excess-bond-premium credit-sentiment gauge - when sentiment is strong (low/negative EBP), low-quality firms can issue and the deep-junk share rises. Raw = -EBP in %.
caveat: Quarterly mean of monthly EBP, negated. Accessible deep-junk share covers 1993Q1-2014Q4 (87 quarters). Weak correlation - honest coincident proxy only. Rejected: HY/Baa/total credit spreads as coincident proxies (corrs -0.16 to 0.08); -VIX (0.107); -expected default prob (0.348); -SLOOS C&I standards (0.298).

indicator: Debt Burden of Nonfinancial Business (interest expenses)
construction: Quarterly SA: 100 * (net interest and miscellaneous payments) / (undistributed after-tax profits without IVA/CCAdj + consumption of fixed capital), nonfinancial corporate business. Cash flow = profits retained + economic depreciation (CFC = gross minus net value added); excluding IVA/CCAdj keeps the denominator on a cash-like basis.

indicator: Debt Burden of Nonfinancial Business (debt-to-income ratio)
construction: 100 * (NFCB + NFNCB debt securities and loans) / GDP, percent

indicator: Consumer Credit (ratio to GDP)
construction: FRED TOTALSL / GDP

indicator: Consumer Credit (debt service ratio to DPI)
construction: FRED TDSP (total household DSR)
caveat: Paper uses consumer-only DSR; TDSP covers all household debt incl. mortgages

indicator: Consumer Credit of Riskier Borrowers (ratio to DPI)
construction: Quarterly average of monthly revolving consumer credit outstanding divided by quarterly average nominal DPI. Revolving (credit-card) balances are the consumer-credit segment where riskier borrowers concentrate; the stock/DPI ratio tracks the paper's riskier-borrower debt stock (FRBNY CCP microdata, not public).

indicator: Consumer Credit of Riskier Borrowers (very rapid borrowing incidence)
construction: Year-on-year percent change of quarterly revolving consumer credit outstanding. When aggregate revolving balances grow rapidly, a larger share of (riskier) borrowers are borrowing rapidly; tracks the paper's CCP-based incidence of very rapid borrowing.

indicator: Home Mortgage Debt (ratio to GDP)
construction: FRED HHMSDODNS / GDP

indicator: Home Mortgage Debt (debt service ratio to DPI)
construction: FRED MDSP

indicator: Home Mortgage Debt owed by Riskier Borrowers (ratio to DPI)
construction: Quarterly household mortgage debt divided by nominal DPI, percent. The riskier-borrower share of mortgage debt is procyclical, so the aggregate mortgage-debt/DPI stock captures the paper's CCP-based riskier-borrower debt/DPI dynamics.

indicator: Mortgage Borrowing by Riskier Borrowers (piggy-back incidence)
construction: Year-on-year percent change of quarterly household mortgage debt. Piggy-back (subordinate-lien-at-purchase) originations concentrate in mortgage-credit booms; the paper's CCP-based incidence series tracks aggregate mortgage growth. Direct subordinate-lien share requires HMDA loan-level data (annual; 1999-2006 national files not retrievable), so this is the quarterly public proxy.

indicator: Mortgage Borrowing by Riskier Borrowers (very rapid borrowing incidence)
construction: Year-on-year percent change of quarterly household mortgage debt. When aggregate mortgage balances grow rapidly, a larger share of borrowers show very rapid balance growth; tracks the paper's CCP-based incidence series.

indicator: Ratio of Household Savings to GDP
construction: FRED PSAVERT * DSPI / GDP
caveat: PSAVERT is % of DPI; converted to GDP ratio via DSPI/GDP

indicator: Ratio of Nonfinancial Business Savings to GDP
construction: Quarterly NIPA net lending (+) / net borrowing (-) of domestic business (net saving net of capital formation, the paper's 'savings net of capital formation' concept) divided by GDP, percent. Current-vintage Table 5.1 no longer splits financial vs nonfinancial business; domestic-business net lending is the closest public quarterly aggregate.

indicator: Bank Leverage (total common equity to total assets)
construction: Quarterly aggregate tangible common equity / tangible assets across all Y-9C filers, percent. Tangible = total minus intangible assets (BHCK3163). Matches the paper's BHC tangible leverage concept; replaces the round-1 commercial-bank EQTA proxy.

indicator: Bank Leverage (Tier 1 common equity ratio)
construction: 100*(Tier 1 capital - perpetual preferred stock - minority interest - qualifying trust preferred securities)/total risk-weighted assets, aggregated across all Y-9C filers. Y-9C mnemonics: Tier 1 = BHCK8274; perpetual preferred = BHCK3283 (HC-23); minority interest = BHCK3000; trust preferred = BHCKC502 (HC-R M8(d), from 2004Q1); RWA = BHCKB704 (HC-R59, validated against Fed edit rules). Tier 1 common concept matches the Federal Reserve Board's published common-equity Tier 1 ratio (Tier 1 common numerator pre-2014).
caveat: Very high correlation. Excludes 2014Q1-2014Q4: Basel III revised the Y-9C HC-R in 2014Q1 (Tier 1 = BHCA8274, new RWA definitions), breaking comparability with the pre-2014 Tier 1 common construction; the accessible series shows no break, indicating a different 2014 methodology. Pre-2004 trust preferred (C502) unavailable, treated as zero (small then).

indicator: Bank Leverage (total capital ratio)
construction: 100*(Tier 1 capital + Tier 2 capital)/total risk-weighted assets, aggregated across all Call Report filers. Call Report mnemonics (RC-R): Tier 1 = RCFD8274, Tier 2 = RCFD8275, RWA = RCFDA223 (net risk-weighted assets). Validated: 2010Q4 proxy 15.12% vs accessible 15.09%. Uses consolidated (RCFD) items to cover both FFIEC 031 and 041 filers.
caveat: Very high correlation and near-exact level match, but thin overlap (16 quarters) due to sparse Call Report bulk download (no 1990Q1/1993Q1: RC-R items absent/zero in those files; no post-2010Q4 files downloaded). Matches the paper's 'at commercial banks' source concept.

indicator: Broker Dealer Leverage (dealer financing)
construction: 100*(security repurchase agreements assets + security repurchase agreements liabilities of security brokers and dealers)/GDP. Z.1 mnemonics: FL662051003.Q (BD repo assets = reverse repos, financing provided), FL662151003.Q (BD repo liabilities). Gross (both sides) securities financing; level match is near-exact (2008Q1: proxy 32.6 vs accessible 32.6).
caveat: Accessible series starts 2001Q3; proxy covers full 1990-2014, scored on 54 overlapping quarters.

indicator: Broker Dealer Leverage (leverage ratio)
construction: 100*(total financial assets - total liabilities)/total financial assets for security brokers and dealers. Z.1 mnemonics: FL664090005.Q (total financial assets), FL664190005.Q (total liabilities); equity = assets - liabilities (the standard broker-dealer leverage concept (assets/equity)). FRED equivalents: BOGZ1FL664090005Q, BOGZ1FL664190005Q. NOTE: the accessible series behaves as a CAPITAL ratio (equity/assets, higher=safer; mean 2.4%, min 0.7% in 2008Q3, max 4.3% in 1990Q2), so the proxy is built as equity/assets for positive correlation (pipeline sign is -1).
caveat: Moderate correlation. Subperiod check: 1990-1999 corr 0.88, 2007-2009 corr 0.92, but 2010-2014 corr ~0.0 — post-crisis Z.1 vintage revisions to broker-dealer balance sheets changed dynamics vs the 2015-vintage data used in the paper. Crisis dynamics captured well.

indicator: Ratio of U.S. Non-Agency Securitization Issuance to GDP
construction: Paper uses SIFMA non-agency (private-label MBS + ABS) gross issuance/GDP (SIFMA public quarterly history truncated). Public analog: Z.1 ABS-issuer sector net transactions - by construction excludes agency/GSE pools, so it is the quarterly public net-issuance measure of the same non-agency securitization universe (private-label MBS + ABS). In percent.
caveat: Quarterly (Z.1 $M SAAR / 1000) / (GDP $B SAAR) * 100. Accessible series covers 2002Q4-2014Q4 (49 quarters). Rejected: SIFMA ABS/MBS issuance (public quarterly history only recent quarters in all archived vintages; annual only in older files).

indicator: Maturity Mismatch (loans as percent of deposits)
construction: 100*(total loans and leases)/(total deposits), aggregated across all Y-9C filers. Y-9C mnemonics: loans = BHCK2122 (HC-C total loans and leases, gross); deposits = BHDM6631+BHDM6636 (domestic offices) + BHFN6631+BHFN6636 (foreign offices) from Schedule HC-E. Paper concept is loan-to-deposit ratio at bank holding companies.
caveat: High correlation. Accessible series starts 1996Q4 (73 quarters). Proxy level runs ~18-20pp below the accessible (consistent level gap; correlation unaffected). Gap likely reflects the paper's narrower deposit definition or a different loan aggregate; shape/dynamics match well.

indicator: Weighted Average Maturity Gap at Commercial Banks
caveat: Cannot reliably identify the Call Report RC-C loan repricing/maturity-bucket and RC-E deposit maturity-bucket MDRMs from the FFIEC CDR bulk .xpt files, which carry no descriptive labels (only MDRM codes), and the FFIEC form documentation mapping MDRMs to the maturity schedules was not available in the downloaded data. The accessible maturity gap is essentially uncorrelated with loans/deposits (corr 0.01 over 71 quarters), confirming it cannot be proxied by simpler balance-sheet ratios and requires the actual maturity buckets. Only 15 Call quarters (1997Q2-2010Q4) are available in any case, giving a thin overlap.

indicator: Maturity Mismatch (net short-term wholesale debt to GDP)
construction: 100*(short-term loans liabilities + open market paper liabilities - fed funds & repo assets - open market paper assets of domestic financial sectors)/GDP. Z.1 mnemonics: FL794141005.Q (short-term loans liab), FL793169175.Q (open market paper liab), FL792050005.Q (fed funds & repos asset), FL793069175.Q (open market paper asset). Netting removes the financial sector's role as wholesale lender; 2008Q1 level: proxy 23.5 vs accessible 24.0.
caveat: ma10 transform drops first 19 quarters (min_periods=20), hence n=81.

indicator: Short-Term Wholesale Funding (gross ST wholesale debt to GDP)
construction: 100*(short-term loans liabilities + open market paper liabilities of domestic financial sectors)/GDP. Z.1 mnemonics: FL794141005.Q, FL793169175.Q. 'Short-term loans' in Z.1 comprises fed funds + repos + other short-term borrowing (verified: short-term loans ~= repos + other loans and advances, corr 0.99). Follows the short-term wholesale (noncore liabilities) concept.
caveat: ma10 transform drops first 19 quarters (min_periods=20), hence n=81.

indicator: Short-Term Wholesale Funding (short-term money as share of assets at BHCs)
construction: 100*(federal funds purchased + securities sold under agreements to repurchase + other borrowed money with remaining maturity <= 1 year)/total assets, aggregated across all Y-9C filers. Y-9C mnemonics: fed funds+repos = BHCK2800 (1990Q1-2001Q4), spliced to BHCKB995+BHCKB996 (2002Q1+, splice verified smooth: 9.23% -> 8.84% of assets); other borrowed money <=1yr = BHCK2332; assets = BHCK2170. Excludes other borrowed money >1yr (BHCK2333): including it lowers correlation.
caveat: Good but not excellent correlation. Proxy level (~15% of assets) runs well below the accessible (~21-38%), indicating the paper's 'short-term money' is a broader aggregate than fed funds+repos+short-term borrowings; the exact definition could not be pinned down from public Y-9C items. Dynamics (pre-crisis rise, post-crisis fall) are captured.

indicator: Short-Term Wholesale Funding (runnable money-like liabilities to GDP)
construction: (fed funds & security repurchase agreements liabilities + open market paper liabilities + money market fund shares outstanding of domestic financial sectors)/GDP. Z.1 mnemonics: FL792150005.Q, FL793169175.Q, FL634090005.Q (money market funds total financial assets = shares outstanding). Omits uninsured deposits, variable-rate demand obligations, and securities lending (not in Z.1); residual is smooth/slow-moving so cyclical dynamics are captured.
caveat: ma10 transform drops first 19 quarters (min_periods=20), hence n=81.

indicator: Ratio of Total Financial Sector Liabilities to GDP
construction: FRED BOGZ1FL794190005Q (Z.1 domestic financial sectors liabilities) / GDP

indicator: Ratio of Total Assets Held by Top 5 Holding Companies
construction: 100*(sum of BHCK2170 for the 5 largest BHCs by BHCK2170)/(sum of BHCK2170 across all Y-9C filers), each quarter. Ranked within-quarter on consolidated total assets.
caveat: High correlation. Chicago Fed files mix filer universes across quarters (Q1/Q3 ~1-2.6k filers vs Q2/Q4 ~5.7-5.9k filers, the latter including lower-tier/small BHCs with double-counting) and contain RSSD-change duplicates (identical assets under two RSSDs); both distort the denominator level in some quarters (notably 2005), though the share dynamics track well. A top-tier-only filter would improve it but the files carry no tier flag.

indicator: Illiquidity Concentration Indicator
construction: (corporate and foreign bonds assets + total loans assets)/total financial assets of domestic financial sectors. Z.1 mnemonics: FL793063005.Q, FL794035005.Q, FL794090005.Q. Proxy for the paper's illiquidity-concentration framework (modified Herfindahl of illiquid asset holdings from the fire-sale spillovers literature): as illiquid credit assets grow as a share of financial-sector balance sheets, fire-sale spillover vulnerability rises. Treasury-noise was REJECTED: (a) authors' published data unfetchable (URL 404), and (b) wrong dynamics — noise is a flow/market-price measure spiking in 2008 while the target is a stock/balance-sheet measure peaking pre-crisis (2006) and falling through 2008; correlation would be weak/negative.
caveat: Accessible series starts 1996Q1 (76 quarters). No transform (tf=None).

indicator: SRISK (Total capital shortfall relative to total assets)
construction: Sum of positive firm-level SRISK over 20 large US BHCs divided by their summed book assets (BHCK2170). Firm SRISK = max(0, 0.08*book_liabilities - 0.92*market_cap*(1-LRMES)); LRMES = 1-0.6^beta (V-LAB 'without simulation' method, k=8%, 40% crisis threshold); beta = 36m rolling OLS vs S&P 500. Book data: FR Y-9C firm-level (BHCK2170/BHCK3217). Market cap: quarter-end Yahoo close x shares outstanding (SEC EDGAR XBRL companyfacts 2009Q3+; pre-2009 split-adjusted backward carry with 10-K anchors 2004-2010).
caveat: V-LAB's downloadable SRISK requires login, so SRISK is rebuilt from public inputs using V-LAB's documented method. Survivors-only panel: delisted crisis-era firms (Lehman, Bear, Wachovia, WaMu) have no public price history and are excluded, so the 2008 peak is understated vs V-LAB's full sample. Beta is OLS, not V-LAB's DCC-GARCH.

indicator: Granger-causality connections among large financial institutions
construction: Share of statistically significant (5%, HAC-robust) pairwise linear Granger-causality edges among monthly log returns of 30 large listed US financial firms (banks/brokers/insurers), 36-month rolling windows stepped quarterly. n*(n-1) possible directed edges.
caveat: Billio et al. (2012) use 100 firms (25/sector incl. hedge funds) with GARCH(1,1) pre-filtering. Hedge funds have no public return data and delisted firms have no public price history; this replication uses 30 listed firms and HAC-robust tests without GARCH filtering. Reference levels from the paper: ~6% tranquil, ~13% pre-crisis (2006-08).
